module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Toronto spaces

A *Toronto space* is a topological space
which is homeomorphic to all of its subspaces of same cardinality.

It is conjectured that every T2, Toronto space is discrete.
W.R. Brian proved that this holds under GCH.

*References:*
 - [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto_space)
 - [The Toronto problem](https://wrbrian.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/01/thetorontoproblem.pdf) by *W.R. Brian*
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Toronto

open Cardinal

variable (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X]

/-- A *Toronto space* is a topological space
which is homeomorphic to all of its subspaces of same cardinality.
-/
class TorontoSpace where
  toronto : ∀ ⦃Y : Set X⦄, #Y = #X → Y ≃ₜ X

/-- Every finite space is Toronto, since
the only subspace with same cardinality is the space itself.
-/
@[category test, AMS 54]
instance Finite.torontoSpace [Finite X] : TorontoSpace X where
  toronto := by
    intro Y hY
    have eq : Y = Set.univ := by
      refine (Set.eq_univ_iff_ncard Y).mpr ?_
      have : Y.ncard = (#↑Y).toNat := by
        exact rfl
      rw [this, hY]
      exact rfl
    rw [eq]
    exact Homeomorph.Set.univ X

/-- Any T2, Toronto space is discrete. -/
@[category research open, AMS 54]
theorem DiscreteTopology.of_t2_of_torontoSpace [T2Space X] [TorontoSpace X] :
    DiscreteTopology X := by
  sorry

-- TODO: Add implication that this holds under the GCH

end Toronto

reformulations.difference: `TorontoSpace X` is a data-carrying class (Type-valued): a function that returns a chosen homeomorphism `↥Y ≃ₜ X` for every `Y : Set X` with `#Y = #X`. It ranges over all full-cardinality subspaces, including `X` itself. The sources state a property: Brian says Y ⊆ X and |Y| = |X| ⇒ Y ≅ X; Wikipedia says 'homeomorphic to every proper subspace of the same cardinality'.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: By choice, `Nonempty (TorontoSpace X) ↔ ∀ Y : Set X, #Y = #X → Nonempty (Y ≃ₜ X)`, which is Brian's definition. The case `Y = univ` always holds via `Homeomorph.Set.univ`, so this is equivalent to Wikipedia's proper-subspace wording. The main theorem quantifies universally over the instance, so it is equivalent to the Prop-level conjecture. Proved sorry-free in /workspace/review/scratch3.lean: `nonempty_torontoSpace_iff`, `isToronto_iff_wiki`, `statement_iff`.

reformulations.difference: The Lean statement covers T2 Toronto spaces of every cardinality: finite, countable and uncountable. Wikipedia frames the problem for uncountable spaces only ('asks for an uncountable Toronto Hausdorff space that is not discrete').
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Finite T2 spaces are discrete. Countably infinite Hausdorff Toronto spaces are discrete (Brian, Cor. 6.2; Wikipedia). I formalised this sorry-free as `countable_t2_toronto_discrete` in /workspace/review/scratch4.lean. The proof finds an open set with infinite complement, then an isolated point, and splits on whether the set of isolated points is finite (contradiction) or infinite (X is homeomorphic to it, hence discrete). From it, `all_iff_uncountable` proves the all-cardinalities statement ↔ its restriction to uncountable X.

reformulations.difference: The sources pose a question. Wikipedia asks for an example; Brian asks whether it is consistent with ZFC to have an infinite Hausdorff non-discrete Toronto space; the original problem asks whether every Hausdorff Toronto space of size ℵ₁ is discrete. The Lean asserts non-existence as a plain `research open` theorem, not as `answer(sorry) ↔ ...`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Brian's Proposition 2.6: 'If the GCH holds then every Hausdorff Toronto space (of any size) is discrete.' So the Lean statement holds in any model of GCH, and ZFC (and Lean, assuming its foundations are consistent with GCH) cannot prove that a counterexample exists. Only two resolutions are possible: (a) a ZFC proof of the Lean statement, or (b) a consistent counterexample, which makes the Lean statement independent, not false. `answer(False)` could never be proved, so `answer(sorry) ↔ P` would carry no more content than P. Proving P is exactly the negative resolution of the source's question. The repository states other ZFC-level set-theoretic topology problems the same way (e.g. Paper/CardinalityLindelof.lean).

sources_consulted: https://wrbrian.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/01/thetorontoproblem.pdf (W.R. Brian, The Toronto problem; full text read: definition, abstract, Thm 2.4, Cor 2.5, Prop 2.6, Thm 6.1, Cor 6.2, Prop 6.3)
https://wrbrian.wordpress.com/research/ (publication record: Topology and its Applications 162 (2014) 76-90)
http://matwbn.icm.edu.pl/ksiazki/fm/fm163/fm16324.pdf (Gruenhage & Moore, Countable Toronto spaces, Fund. Math. 163 (2000): statement of Steprāns' Toronto problem and its status)
https://api.zbmath.org/v1/document/_search (zbMATH records/reviews: Brian 2014, Soukup 2004 'A piecewise Toronto space', Coleman 1997, Hernández 1998, Tallafha–Shakhatreh 2001, Shelah–Steprāns 1994)
https://archive.org/details/openproblemsinto0000unse/page/15 (Open Problems in Topology; lending-restricted, no text available)
review.notes:
No defects found. Details:

1. Scope. Steprāns' original Toronto problem (Open Problems in Topology, 1990) is about spaces of size ℵ₁; Brian's abstract, Gruenhage–Moore and Soukup's zbMATH review all phrase it that way. The file states the general all-cardinalities version. That is what both cited sources present as open: Wikipedia says 'uncountable', and Brian writes 'whether it is consistent with ZFC to have an infinite Hausdorff non-discrete Toronto space'. The docstring's GCH remark matches Brian's Prop. 2.6, which is also about all sizes. The Lean statement is stronger than the ℵ₁ question, so a ZFC proof of the ℵ₁ case alone would not settle it. An ℵ₁ variant (`#X = ℵ₁`) would be a natural addition, but its absence is not a misformalization.

2. Wording. The module docstring says 'It is conjectured that every T2, Toronto space is discrete.' None of the sources conjectures an answer; they ask a question. Soukup's 2004 'piecewise Toronto space' is described as 'almost' answering the question positively, i.e. in favour of existence. This leaves the mathematics intact: as explained under reformulations, P is the only direction ZFC could prove. So I did not file it as a finding.

3. Status. `research open` agrees with the sources. Brian (2014) calls the general question open. zbMATH lists nothing after 2014 that resolves it, and the current Wikipedia revision presents it as open. arXiv, Semantic Scholar-search and OpenAlex were rate-limited from this sandbox, so the status check rests on zbMATH, Wikipedia, Brian's publication page and one Semantic Scholar citation lookup. I could not read Steprāns' chapter directly (the archive.org copy is lending-only); its wording is taken from Gruenhage–Moore, Brian and the zbMATH reviews.

4. Lean checks (all sorry-free, only standard axioms), in /workspace/review:
- Discrete spaces and indiscrete spaces are Toronto, so the hypotheses can be satisfied, including by an infinite T2 space (discrete ℕ).
- The empty type and finite T2 spaces satisfy the conclusion trivially.
- The data-carrying class is equivalent to the Prop definition and to Wikipedia's proper-subspace wording.
- Countable Hausdorff Toronto spaces are discrete, so the all-cardinalities statement ↔ its uncountable restriction.

The docstring's claim 'W.R. Brian proved that this holds under GCH' is accurate: Prop. 2.6, which Brian credits to himself.
